entities.name: Spurius Nautius Rutilus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Spurius Nautius Rutilus was a Roman aristocrat of the Patrician gens Nautia, who played a crucial role in shaping the early 5th century BC Roman Republic.

As Consul of Rome in 488 BC, he collaborated with Sextus Furius, and later served in the Roman Senate, contributing to the development of Roman law and governance.

His legacy extended beyond his own lifetime, as he influenced the Roman Republic's expansion into the Mediterranean region, particularly in the wake of the devastating Peloponnesian War.

"The gods have ordained that Rome shall be a great empire," he is said to have remarked, a sentiment that would become a defining mantra of Roman imperial ambitions.
